key_insight: An automated workflow can discover kinetically significant reaction mechanisms in complex condensed-phase chemistry without relying on human intuition, while linking molecular reactions to space- and time-resolved product formation.
engineering_relevance: This enables better prediction and control of radiation- and photo-induced degradation, crosslinking, and deprotection in materials such as EUV photoresists and other reactive thin films.
method: High-throughput DFT generates candidate species and reaction energetics.
Automated network construction with plausibility filtering and stochastic pathway sampling identifies likely reactions.
Reaction-diffusion simulations track species explicitly in space and time across nanoscale domains.
evidence_signal: In a 15.5-nm radiolytic spur model, the workflow started from over 3,300 species and millions of candidate reactions and reproduced experimentally detected products across femtosecond-to-nanosecond timescales.
watch_item: The approach is computationally intensive and depends on the completeness of the candidate species/reaction space and the quality of the filtering rules and DFT energetics.
paper_title: Discovering Kinetically Significant Reaction Mechanisms Beyond Chemical Intuition in Condensed-Phase Radiolysis
